newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, Escondida strike over.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, Escondida strike over.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer on Friday, despite a further rise in LME stocks and a return to work by strikers at Escondida mine in Chile amid signs of a settlement at the country's other dispute-hit producer, Quebrada Blanca.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said the two disputes were a "non-event" to start with as there was no real loss of production.
Other dealers said the disputes at the two mines had already been written into the copper price.
On Friday Escondida and its 350-member union signed a two-year collective wage agreement, and the union said strikers were returning to work.
Quebrada Blanca management and unions were due to meet late Friday in a bid to agree on a new wage contract at the mine where workers have been on strike for three days.
LME stocks rose 2,175 tonnes Friday to 147,925 tonnes.

July COMEX copper quietly traded in a narrow range for most of the day, ending 0.40 cent firmer at 110.25 cents per pound, after ranging between 110.50 and 108.90 cents. Spot May went out 0.80 cent firmer at 111.70 cents.
The LME cash to three months spread or backwardation, the driving force behind recent sharp price movements, remained stable for much of the day, ending at $68/$73.

"The spreads could well show some renewed strength in the next couple of weeks as there is still some tightness there," O'Neill said. "The weakness we had this week was more of a consolidation rather than any trend change. The solid demand structure remains in place."
Trading Friday was cautious and light on LME ahead of a long weekend in the U.K. with the London exchange shut Monday.
